    1.0 Preprocess and align the E15.5 Xenium brain¶

    This notebook prepares the Xenium E15.5 whole-brain dataset for 3D visualization with Celldega. The visualization notebooks that follow (2.0 CellCloud, 2.1 NeighborhoodCloud, 3.0 composition + Landscape) read what is written here.

    The experiment¶

    Whole-brain spatial transcriptomics of a mouse embryo at E15.5 (female). The brain was cut into 44 coronal sections, ordered from the front of the brain (slice 1, anterior) to the back (slice 44, posterior). The sections were placed on four Xenium slides and profiled with the 10x Xenium platform and its 480-gene panel, which reads out transcripts at subcellular resolution. Cells were segmented from the images, which gives each cell a position (in µm) and a gene-count vector.

    Consecutive slices are stacked 100 µm apart to rebuild the brain in 3D. After quality control the dataset holds about 3.8 million cells.

    What this notebook does¶

    1. Load the cells of all 44 slices (positions in µm, raw counts for the 480 genes).
    2. Cluster all cells together with Leiden, so a cluster means the same thing in every slice.
    3. Drop one slice (not shown) that does not align well and has poor clusters.
    4. Align the remaining 43 slices in 3D with Celldega, in two stages:
      • Centroids: one landmark per (slice, cluster) at the cluster's centroid, then a rigid Procrustes fit chained out from the middle slice.
      • Neighborhood overlap: one alpha shape per (slice, cluster); each slice's rigid pose is refined to maximize the overlap of matching shapes in nearby slices.
    5. Write the DegaFiles that the visualization notebooks load.

    Helpers¶

    Two small functions, defined here so the notebook is self-contained.

    • side_view_coords re-expresses the aligned cells for CellCloud. Its orbit camera always spins around the vertical (data-Z) axis, so the stack goes along data-X (anterior on the left, posterior on the right) and the dorsal-ventral axis along Z (dorsal up).
    • write_point_cloud_genes writes the counts of every gene as one small file per gene, so that the viewer can color the 3D cloud by any gene.
    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    def side_view_coords(xy_um, stack_um, flip_dv=True):
    """Re-express aligned cells so CellCloud orbits *around* the brain.

    CellCloud uses deck.gl's ``OrbitView`` with ``orbitAxis="Z"``: left-right drag spins the
    scene around data-Z. The stacking axis therefore goes to data-X (anterior on the left),
    the dorsal-ventral axis to data-Z, and the box is centered on the origin:
    ``(x, y, stack) -> (stack, -x, -y)``, a proper rotation (no mirroring). ``flip_dv`` turns
    the brain upside down so dorsal is up.
    """
    xy_um = np.asarray(xy_um, float)
    stack_um = np.asarray(stack_um, float)
    pts = np.column_stack([xy_um, stack_um])
    center = (pts.min(axis=0) + pts.max(axis=0)) / 2
    x, y, s = xy_um[:, 0] - center[0], xy_um[:, 1] - center[1], stack_um - center[2]
    sign = -1.0 if flip_dv else 1.0
    return np.column_stack([s, -x * sign, -y * sign])


def write_point_cloud_genes(h5ad_path, dega_dir, keep_mask, chunk=250_000):
    """Write ``cbg/<gene>.parquet`` + ``meta_gene.parquet`` for a point cloud.

    Streams the raw counts in ``X`` of an h5ad in row chunks. Only cells in ``keep_mask`` (the
    cells written to the cloud) are exported, keyed by cell name.
    """
    from celldega.pre import _create_cluster_colors

    t0 = time.time()
    dega_dir = Path(dega_dir)
    cbg_dir = dega_dir / "cbg"
    if cbg_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(cbg_dir)
    cbg_dir.mkdir(parents=True)

    a = ad.read_h5ad(h5ad_path, backed="r")
    genes = a.var_names.tolist()
    keep_mask = np.asarray(keep_mask, bool)
    kept_rows = np.flatnonzero(keep_mask)
    new_index = np.full(a.n_obs, -1, dtype=np.int64)         # row in the file -> row in the exported table
    new_index[kept_rows] = np.arange(len(kept_rows))
    cell_names = pa.array(a.obs_names[kept_rows].astype(str).tolist(), type=pa.string())
    n_cells = len(kept_rows)

    rows_per_gene = [[] for _ in genes]
    vals_per_gene = [[] for _ in genes]
    for start in range(0, a.n_obs, chunk):
        stop = min(start + chunk, a.n_obs)
        block = a.X[start:stop].tocsc()
        local_new = new_index[start:stop]
        for j in range(len(genes)):
            lo, hi = block.indptr[j], block.indptr[j + 1]
            if hi == lo:
                continue
            r = local_new[block.indices[lo:hi]]
            ok = r >= 0
            if ok.any():
                rows_per_gene[j].append(r[ok].astype(np.int32))
                vals_per_gene[j].append(block.data[lo:hi][ok].astype(np.int32))
        print(f"  scanned {stop:,}/{a.n_obs:,} cells ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
    a.file.close()

    stats = {}
    for j, gene in enumerate(genes):
        if not rows_per_gene[j]:
            continue
        rows = np.concatenate(rows_per_gene[j])
        vals = np.concatenate(vals_per_gene[j])
        rows_per_gene[j] = vals_per_gene[j] = None
        v = vals.astype(np.float64)
        mean = v.sum() / n_cells
        stats[gene] = {
            "mean": mean,
            "std": np.sqrt(max((v**2).sum() / n_cells - mean**2, 0.0)),
            "max": float(vals.max()),
            "non-zero": len(vals) / n_cells,
        }
        pq.write_table(
            pa.table({gene: pa.array(vals), "__index_level_0__": cell_names.take(pa.array(rows))}),
            cbg_dir / f"{gene}.parquet",
            compression="snappy",
        )

    meta_gene = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(stats, orient="index")
    meta_gene["color"] = pd.Series(_create_cluster_colors(meta_gene.index.tolist()), index=meta_gene.index)
    meta_gene = meta_gene.sort_index()
    meta_gene.index.name = None
    meta_gene.to_parquet(dega_dir / "meta_gene.parquet")
    print(f"{len(stats)} genes written, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s total")
    return meta_gene

CellCloud uses deck.gl's ``OrbitView`` with ``orbitAxis="Z"``: left-right drag spins the scene around data-Z. The stacking axis therefore goes to data-X (anterior on the left), the dorsal-ventral axis to data-Z, and the box is centered on the origin: ``(x, y, stack) -> (stack, -x, -y)``, a proper rotation (no mirroring). ``flip_dv`` turns the brain upside down so dorsal is up.     1. Load the cells¶

    Cells are read from the combined AnnData: counts for the 480 genes, positions in µm, the slice number (slice_number, 1 = most anterior) and the Leiden labels. The working copy written here keeps only what the later steps need.

    Slice 13 has a second, separated piece of tissue (the lower half of the section); only the main piece is aligned, and it is flagged as extra_tissue_piece.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    if not CLUSTERED_H5AD.exists():
    with h5py.File(SOURCE_H5AD, "r") as f:
        obs = read_elem(f["obs"])
        var = read_elem(f["var"])
        counts = read_elem(f["layers/counts"]).tocsr()
        spatial = np.asarray(read_elem(f["obsm"]["spatial"]))
        umap = np.asarray(read_elem(f["obsm"]["X_umap"]))

    obs_new = pd.DataFrame(index=obs.index.astype(str))
    obs_new["slice"] = obs["slice_number"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    obs_new["region"] = obs["sample_id"].astype(str).to_numpy()   # Xenium output region
    obs_new["barcode"] = obs_new.index.str.split("_", n=1).str[1]   # cell id inside the region
    for c in ["x", "y", "total_counts", "n_genes_by_counts", "cell_area", "nucleus_area"] + LEIDEN_KEYS:
        obs_new[c] = obs[c].to_numpy()

    is13 = (obs_new["slice"] == 13).to_numpy()
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=0, n_init=10).fit(spatial[is13, 1].reshape(-1, 1))
    extra = np.zeros(len(obs_new), bool)
    extra[np.flatnonzero(is13)[km.labels_ == np.argmax(km.cluster_centers_.ravel())]] = True
    obs_new["extra_tissue_piece"] = extra

    counts.data = np.round(counts.data).astype(np.int32)
    adata = ad.AnnData(X=counts, obs=obs_new, var=pd.DataFrame(index=var.index.astype(str)))
    adata.obsm["spatial"], adata.obsm["X_umap"] = spatial, umap
    for key in LEIDEN_KEYS:                                       # numerically ordered categories + fixed palette
        cats = sorted(adata.obs[key].astype(str).unique(), key=int)
        adata.obs[key] = pd.Categorical(adata.obs[key].astype(str), categories=cats)
        adata.uns[f"{key}_colors"] = list(dega.pre._create_cluster_colors(cats))
    adata.write_h5ad(CLUSTERED_H5AD, compression="lzf")
    del counts, adata

colors = dict(zip(obs[CLUSTER_KEY].cat.categories, adata.uns[f"{CLUSTER_KEY}_colors"]))
adata.file.close()
print(f"{len(obs):,} cells, {obs['slice'].nunique()} slices, {adata.n_vars} genes")

    2. Clusters¶

    All cells from all slices were clustered together with Leiden, using rapids-singlecell, so a cluster means the same thing in every slice. This is what lets the alignment match "the same region" between neighboring slices. We use the leiden_1.0 clusters throughout; the labels are already in the AnnData.

    3. Drop the slice that does not align¶

    One slice is left out of the 3D stack: it is a small fragment at the end of the series that barely overlaps its neighbor and has poor clusters. Its position in the stack is left empty, so the remaining slices keep their true spacing.

slice_ids = sorted(cells.obs["slice_order"].unique())

    3,787,366 of 3,828,568 cells kept, 43 slices

    4. Align, stage 1: cluster centroids + Procrustes¶

    dega.align.calc_landmarks gives one landmark per (slice, cluster) at the cluster's centroid. A tissue-center landmark is added per slice. calc_alignment_transform then fits a rigid transform for each slice to its neighbors (within alignment_window slices), chain-walking out from the middle slice. Because the same cluster appears in neighboring slices, its centroid is a landmark that should land on top of itself after alignment.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    landmarks = dega.align.calc_landmarks(cells, cluster_key=CLUSTER_KEY, slice_attr="slice_order")

rows = []
for s in slice_ids:
    xy = cells.obsm["spatial"][cells.obs["slice_order"].to_numpy() == s]
    (x_lo, x_hi), (y_lo, y_hi) = np.percentile(xy[:, 0], [1, 99]), np.percentile(xy[:, 1], [1, 99])
    rows.append({"slice_order": s, "label": "tissue_center", "x": (x_lo + x_hi) / 2,
                 "y": (y_lo + y_hi) / 2, "count": np.nan, "source": "manual"})
landmarks = pd.concat([landmarks, pd.DataFrame(rows)], ignore_index=True)
landmarks.to_parquet(OUT_DIR / "centroid_landmarks.parquet")

procrustes = dega.align.calc_alignment_transform(
    landmarks, slice_attr="slice_order", reference=len(slice_ids) // 2, method="procrustes", **PROCRUSTES_KW,
)
procrustes.save(OUT_DIR / "procrustes_transform")
print(f"{len(landmarks):,} landmarks, reference slice index {procrustes.reference}")

    5. Align, stage 2: neighborhood overlap¶

    A neighborhood is the alpha shape of all cells of one cluster in one slice, computed in each slice's native frame. neighborhood_alignment starts from the Procrustes pose and nudges each slice (a bounded rotation and translation) to maximize the overlap of matching neighborhoods in nearby slices. It returns the combined transform, which is applied to native coordinates.

    6. Did the second stage help?¶

    For each pair of adjacent slices: the mean over clusters of the intersection-over-union (IoU) of the two slices' alpha shapes after alignment. Higher means matching regions overlap better.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    native = _load_slice_geometries(shapes, "slice_id", "cluster_id", None)
alignments = {"centroids": procrustes.transforms, "neighborhood": neighborhood.transforms}


def adjacent_iou(transforms):
    out = []
    for a, b in zip(slice_ids[:-1], slice_ids[1:]):
        ious = []
        for cl in set(native[a]) & set(native[b]):
            ga = shapely.transform(native[a][cl], transforms[a].apply)
            gb = shapely.transform(native[b][cl], transforms[b].apply)
            inter = ga.intersection(gb).area
            union = ga.area + gb.area - inter
            ious.append(inter / union if union > 0 else 0.0)
        out.append(np.mean(ious) if ious else np.nan)
    return out


iou = pd.DataFrame({"slice": slice_ids[:-1]})
for name, t in alignments.items():
    iou[name] = adjacent_iou(t)
iou.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "adjacent_iou.csv", index=False)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.5))
ax.plot(iou["slice"], iou["centroids"], "o-", ms=3, label="centroids (Procrustes)")
ax.plot(iou["slice"], iou["neighborhood"], "o-", ms=3, label="+ neighborhood overlap")
ax.set(xlabel="slice (IoU with the next slice)", ylabel="mean cluster IoU", ylim=(0, 1))
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
iou[["centroids", "neighborhood"]].mean().round(3)

    7. Apply both alignments to every cell¶

    The position along the stack is (slice - reference) * 100 µm, so the dropped slice leaves a gap instead of shifting the later slices.

    8. Write the CellCloud DegaFiles¶

    CellCloud is a 3D point cloud of every cell. Its orbit camera always spins around the vertical (data-Z) axis, so side_view_coords puts the stack along data-X (anterior on the left, posterior on the right) and the dorsal-ventral axis along Z (dorsal up). Left-right drag then swings the brain around to its front and back.

    Draw order. CellCloud draws points in file order and does not depth-sort them, so whatever is written last is painted on top. The initial camera of 2.0_Viz_CellCloud (rotation_x=20, rotation_orbit=-25) sits on the posterior side, so the cells are written anterior first, posterior last: the slices nearest the camera cover the ones behind them. Orbiting to the other side shows the stack the wrong way round until the order is reversed.

    Both alignments are written as named variants of one directory (neighborhood is the default; centroids can be switched to), together with the counts of all 480 genes.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    if CELL_CLOUD_DIR.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(CELL_CLOUD_DIR)

draw_order = np.argsort(slices, kind="stable")        # posterior slices last, on top for the posterior camera
for name in ["neighborhood", "centroids"]:
    xyz = side_view_coords(aligned_xy[name], stack_um)[draw_order]
    a = ad.AnnData(obs=cells.obs.iloc[draw_order][[CLUSTER_KEY]].copy())
    a.obs["Z"] = xyz[:, 2]
    a.obsm["spatial"] = xyz[:, :2]
    a.uns[f"{CLUSTER_KEY}_colors"] = [colors[c] for c in a.obs[CLUSTER_KEY].cat.categories]
    dega.align.write_alignment_point_cloud(
        a, CELL_CLOUD_DIR, alignment_name=name, z_key="Z", cluster_key=CLUSTER_KEY, write_genes=False, overwrite=True,
    )
    print(f"wrote alignment '{name}'")

    9. Write the NeighborhoodCloud DegaFiles¶

    NeighborhoodCloud draws one precomputed alpha-shape polygon per (slice, cluster), which stays light however many cells there are; real cells are fetched when a cluster is selected. It uses the neighborhood-aligned positions, with at most 60,000 randomly chosen cells per slice for the polygons and the cell scatter.

    In [13]:
    Copied! 
    MAX_CELLS_PER_SLICE = 60_000

pick = (aligned.assign(i=np.arange(len(aligned))).groupby("slice_order", group_keys=False)
        .apply(lambda d: d.sample(min(len(d), MAX_CELLS_PER_SLICE), random_state=0))["i"].sort_values().to_numpy())

categories = list(colors)
adata_nbhd = ad.AnnData(obs=cells.obs.iloc[pick][[CLUSTER_KEY]].astype(str))
adata_nbhd.obs["slice_id"] = slices[pick].astype(int)
adata_nbhd.obs["Z"] = stack_um[pick]
xy = aligned_xy["neighborhood"][pick]
adata_nbhd.obsm["spatial"] = np.column_stack([xy[:, 0], -xy[:, 1]])     # dorsal up

meta_cluster = pd.DataFrame({"color": pd.Series(colors), "count": adata_nbhd.obs[CLUSTER_KEY].value_counts()}).dropna()

if NBHD_CLOUD_DIR.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(NBHD_CLOUD_DIR)
dega.align.write_nbhd_cloud(
    adata_nbhd, NBHD_CLOUD_DIR, cluster_attr=CLUSTER_KEY, slice_attr="slice_id", z_attr="Z", alphas=[ALPHA_UM],
    meta_cluster=meta_cluster, max_cell_scatter=50_000, compute_gene_nbhds=False, save_genes=False, progress_every=10,
)
print(f"wrote {NBHD_CLOUD_DIR}")

    # write_alignment_point_cloud / write_nbhd_cloud assign the palette to the clusters in their own order, so
# set the cluster -> color table explicitly: the same colors as the UMAP, Landscape and Clustergram.
counts_by_cluster = cells.obs[CLUSTER_KEY].astype(str).value_counts()
for d in (CELL_CLOUD_DIR, NBHD_CLOUD_DIR):
    meta = pd.read_parquet(d / "cell_clusters" / "meta_cluster.parquet")
    meta.index = meta.index.astype(str)
    meta["color"] = pd.Series(colors).rename(index=str).reindex(meta.index).to_numpy()
    meta["count"] = counts_by_cluster.reindex(meta.index).astype(int).to_numpy()
    meta.to_parquet(d / "cell_clusters" / "meta_cluster.parquet")
